seoTitle: How to Bulk Edit Shopify Prices by Percentage in 2026
metaDescription: Need to raise or lower prices across your whole Shopify store? Here's how to bulk edit by percentage using a pricing app's Create task screen.
intro: Changing prices one product at a time in Shopify works fine for a handful of items, but it falls apart the moment you're running a storewide sale or adjusting margins after a supplier cost change. This guide covers the real path through the Shopify admin and a bulk pricing app — specifically Bulk Price Editor Sami's Create task screen — to apply a percentage increase or decrease across your whole catalog in one action instead of hundreds. It also covers what to check before you apply a change, since a percentage adjustment across every product is hard to reverse cleanly if something's set up wrong.

steps.heading: Start from your Shopify admin home
steps.body: The admin home screen gives you a quick read on recent sessions, total sales, and orders before you touch anything, plus the left-hand navigation you'll use throughout — Products is where individual items and their prices live, while Discounts and Content sit nearby but aren't the same thing as bulk price editing. If you're running a sale, glancing at this dashboard first gives you a sense of current traffic and conversion, which is useful context for deciding how aggressive a price change to run.

image.caption: The Shopify admin dashboard — sessions, sales, and orders at a glance, with Products and the sales channels list in the left-hand navigation.

steps.heading: Use Shopify's built-in bulk editor for simple changes
steps.body: For editing a modest number of products or setting the exact same new price across a small selection, Shopify's own Products page has a built-in bulk editor — select the checkboxes next to the products you want, then use the bulk actions menu to edit fields including price directly in a spreadsheet-style view. This works well for flat, one-off changes but doesn't handle percentage-based math across an entire catalog on its own, which is where a dedicated app comes in.

steps.heading: Install a percentage-based bulk pricing app
steps.body: For a true percentage change — increase everything by 10%, decrease everything by 20% — install an app built for that specific job, such as Bulk Price Editor Sami, Easy by Bulk Editing, or Hextom. These apps add themselves to your admin's left-hand navigation once installed and give you a task-based interface for defining exactly what should change and by how much, rather than editing product by product.

steps.heading: Create a percentage price task
steps.body: Inside the app, Create task is where the actual rule lives: name the task something identifiable like "Bulk increase by 10%," set Field to edit to Price, choose Increase by percentage or Decrease by percentage under Edit method, and enter your value. A Rounding option, set here to round to the nearest .01, keeps the math from producing awkward prices like $10.458, and a Compare at price setting lets you decide whether the app should touch your strikethrough sale pricing as part of the same task or leave it alone.

image.caption: Bulk Price Editor Sami's Create task screen — a named task, Field set to Price, Increase by percentage, a value of 10%, and rounding set to the nearest cent.

steps.heading: Choose when the change takes effect
steps.body: Most of these apps offer a Start time choice between running the task immediately or scheduling it for a specific date and time — useful for lining a price increase up with a supplier cost change or timing a discount to start exactly at midnight on a sale's first day. A Revert time option, when available, is worth using for temporary sales, since it schedules the price to automatically return to normal afterward instead of relying on you remembering to undo it manually.

steps.heading: Test before applying to your whole catalog
steps.body: Before running a percentage task against every product you sell, apply it to a small handful first — a single collection or a few test products — and check the resulting prices look right, including anything affected by the rounding and compare-at settings. This catches mistakes like an inverted increase/decrease setting or an unexpected rounding result while the damage is still limited to a few items instead of your entire store.

faq.question: Can I bulk edit prices without installing an app?
faq.answer: Yes, Shopify's admin has a built-in bulk editor for adjusting prices directly on selected products, though percentage-based automation across a whole catalog typically requires a dedicated app.

faq.question: What's the difference between Bulk Price Editor Sami, Easy by Bulk Editing, and Hextom?
faq.answer: These are different third-party apps that all offer percentage-based bulk pricing tools with a similar task-based workflow, so the right choice depends on which pricing tier and extra features fit your store best.

faq.question: Can I schedule a price increase to happen automatically after a sale ends?
faq.answer: Yes — apps like this typically offer a Revert time option that schedules prices to return to normal automatically after a sale, without manual work.

faq.question: Is it safe to bulk edit prices on a live store?
faq.answer: It's safer to test the change on a small collection or a few products first, since applying a percentage change to your entire catalog without checking rounding and compare-at settings can lead to pricing mistakes that affect real customers.
